verdict: NO-GO for the polygon as drawn. The north 1.5 m of the footprint (V -9.8 to about -11.3, U -53 to -43.5) is seen as walkable floor: the videographer walks along V -9.4 to -9.8 (597.9-598.3 s just inside the edge) and a pedestrian stands at U -48.4, V -10.2 (588.9 s). The southern part (V -11.5 to -17) is never in view in 560-600 s, so this clip neither shows nor rules out an opening there. What the clip does show (anchor ctl-hash): a line of stainless-clad columns at V -11.4 to -12.4 (U -59.5, -52.5 and -44.8, about 7-7.7 m apart; 2 of them inside the footprint) and a waist-high stone ledge with a stainless rail whose west face runs along U -55.6 from V -12.2 to -14.0. Relative to the north wall, the columns are 4.9 m south of it; Naver's 2F stairs/escalator block starts 4.7 m south of Naver's rooms front. [INFERENCE] The ledge and columns may be the guard of an opening south of V ~-11.8 and east of U ~-55.6; this is not confirmed. If Main cuts an opening, move its north edge to V <= -11.8 (the column line) and do not cut north of it.
